T-1 session lifecycle: exactly one connect() per run, used for the domain enumeration and every per-domain query and the connection-table reads, and disconnect() in a finally path so a run that fails mid-way still closes; a run whose disconnect fails reports that outcome explicitly in its result type rather than swallowing it.

T-2/T-3 the closed command set: the concrete management shell commands this transport issues (the domain enumeration, the per-domain object query per queried object type, the connection-table read, and whatever session/context-switch commands those require) are declared ONCE in a single class as a closed list, each with the ten items docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL.md 'Network-device command gate' requires (why required, taxonomy class -- every one of them must be class 0 read --, vendor/platform/shell/context, timeout, retry, max frequency per endpoint, session reuse, unsupported behaviour, secret-bearing output risk, safe telemetry) written as a table in a NEW document docs/design/CP_DISCOVERY_MANAGEMENT_COMMAND_GATE_ENTRIES.md whose status block reads 'DRAFT -- PENDING PRODUCT OWNER GATE APPROVAL' and states plainly it authorizes nothing until approved. A JUnit test asserts every command string the adapter can ever send is a member of that closed list.

FB-2 binding at one site: the adapter parses responses ONLY through ManagementApiFieldBinding.forRole(...).apiField() -- no other production class may contain a concrete field-name string literal. Where the adapter needs a field the 12 existing roles do not cover (for example whatever key identifies a domain in the enumeration, or the address/port/state columns of the connection table), ADD a Role to ManagementApiFieldBinding with an UNVERIFIED entry; never inline it. Every entry stays UNVERIFIED: this movement may not flip any entry to a verified status, because no worker has the measurement (contract status block; FB-2). A JUnit test scans the adapter's production sources for string literals that equal any bound field name outside ManagementApiFieldBinding and fails on a hit.

T-4 no device contact: the only host the adapter ever passes to connect() is the management server's own address given by the caller; every address parsed out of any response is a value inside a RawCandidateInput or a connection-table row and is never used as a ConnectionTarget, never resolved, never probed. A test with a fake DeviceTransport records every ConnectionTarget seen across a full fixture run and asserts exactly one distinct host.

T-5/SB-12/SB-16: the run takes an opaque credentialRef and a trustRuleRef (the existing ConnectSpec shape) and NOTHING secret; if SshCredentialResolver.resolve throws or returns nothing usable, the run is refused with a typed outcome BEFORE connect() is called. No username, password, key or raw response reaches a log line, an exception message or a result object.
T-6: commands are issued strictly sequentially in the one session; no executor, no parallel stream, no per-domain thread.

T-7 raw-evidence law: the raw command output is parsed in memory into RawCandidateInput / channel-state values and then dropped. The result type carries no raw text field and nothing writes a file. A test asserts the run result and every value reachable from it contains no raw response string.

Section 7.4 connection table: CS-6a reduce the table to one state per address, join only addresses that also appear as a candidate's management address in the object-database results, and report nothing for an address with no object; CS-3 take two observations separated by a caller-supplied interval and report 'failing to complete' only when both observations agree, 'in transition' when they disagree, never resolving by recency or preference; CS-6b the channel port is DERIVED from the observed established rows or supplied by configuration -- a test asserts no numeric port literal appears in the adapter's production sources (loopback/zero excluded if you need them); LV-1 to LV-3 no derived liveness value of any kind.

Section 9 check 17 readiness: the run result carries the count of management-plane requests issued so that check 17's arithmetic (one session + one domain enumeration + per domain per queried type the number of pages) can be evaluated by the Product Owner; a fixture test asserts the count equals that formula for a fixture with two domains.

A Product-Owner-runnable entry point WITHOUT an authenticated network surface: one subcommand in the existing ui2 worker main (composition root, where SshExecTransport is already wired) or a documented main class in worker, that takes management host, credentialRef, trustRuleRef and the CS-3 interval, runs one discovery, and prints COUNTS AND SHAPES ONLY per AGENTS.md 'Sensitive identity reporting law': candidates per kind, host-resolution outcomes per kind, cluster links / NOT_EVALUABLE counts, channel-state counts per CS-1 state, request count, and the UNCLASSIFIED/AMBIGUOUS counts of check 7. It prints no name, no address, no domain name, no identifier. This is how section 9 checks 7, 9, 11, 14 to 18 become runnable; this movement does NOT run them.

Fixture-driven tests only, in worker's test tree, with synthetic response texts you invent (no real address, hostname, domain, identifier or object name -- follow platform-core's discovery/cp/Fixtures.java discipline): the T-1 close-on-failure path, the T-2 request-count formula, the T-3 closed-command-set membership, the T-4 single-host assertion, the T-5 refusal-before-contact path, the T-7 no-raw-retention assertion, CS-3's three outcomes, CS-6a's reduction and object-join, CS-6b's no-literal-port scan, and the FB-2 no-inline-field-name scan.
